methods.label: Compare forward angles on the unit circle
methods.explanation:
Cosine is the horizontal coordinate on the unit circle, so the conditions specify starting and ending directions. Within one full turn, \(\cos x=0\) at
\[
x=\frac{\pi}{2}\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{3\pi}{2},
\]
and cosine equals \(\tfrac12\) at \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) and \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\). All other possibilities repeat these directions after full turns.

A positive \(z\) is a counterclockwise rotation from a starting direction to an ending direction. Starting at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), the first ending direction reached is \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\), requiring
\[
\frac{5\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{7\pi}{6}.
\]
Starting at \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\), the first ending direction is again \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\), requiring
\[
\frac{5\pi}{3}-\frac{3\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]
For each starting direction, any later ending direction requires a larger rotation. These two cases cover all possible starting directions, so the smallest positive value is \(\boxed{\frac{\pi}{6}}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\). It is attained by \(x=\frac{3\pi}{2}\).
